focus: Default-on integration: requirements, cost model, risk register

title: Default-on needs a named reader, a phase and an amendment; 030 drops a model as the merge decision and every verdict line says reader=none named.
The live merge is a hermetic zero-network synthesis step in both workflows; a default-on call must degrade byte-identically to today's output.
The origin/main publication guard withholds live pre-commit pairs as unmeasured_unpublished, so default-on with today's guard measures nothing live.
No answer cache by design plus atomic deterministic registry writes means a model in the merge needs a pair-keyed cache with its own identity and invalidation.
323 ms and 65 input tokens per call, 2-3 calls per pair; 124 pairs over 104 runs at ~1.2 per run with a labeled maximum of 10; no cap exists on merge-side pair spend.
Measured risk: 3 of 47 same-calls falsely merged, 4 of 48 same pairs missed, tiebreak caused 2 of those; review count bindings change under collapse even when the verdict class survives.
Integration tiers: T0 zero-call census default-on today; T1 default-on shadow with a named reader; T2 non-collapsing annotation; T3 model-as-collapse stays dropped.
